Gray|the British solo artist|Yazz|other uses|Yaz (disambiguation)|and|Yazoo (disambiguation)}} {{Infobox musical artist | name = Yazoo | image = Vince Clarke and Alison Moyet of Yazoo (1982).jpg | caption = Yazoo in 1982 | landscape = yes | background = group_or_band | alias = Yaz | origin = [[Basildon]], [[Essex]], England | genre = {{hlist|[[Synth-pop]]{{cite web|url= http://www.allmusic.com/album/in-your-room-mw0000789432 |first= David |last= Jeffries |title= Yazoo – In Your Room |website= [[AllMusic]] |access-date= 8 April 2014}}{{cite book|title= Energy Flash: A Journey Through Rave Music and Dance Culture |first= Simon |last= Reynolds |author-link= Simon Reynolds |publisher= [[Faber and Faber]] |url= https://books.google.com/books?id=CXPZyYHLd-kC&pg=PT35 |year= 2013 |isbn= 978-0-571-28914-1}}{{cite web|url= http://www.trouserpress.com/entry.php?a=yazoo_yaz |first1= Karen |last1= Schlosberg |first2= Ira |last2= Robbins |first3= Michael |last3= Zwirn |title= Yazoo (Yaz) |work= [[Trouser Press]] |access-date= 8 April 2014}}|[[New wave music|new wave]]{{Cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=knv3DwAAQBAJ&dq=new+wave+duo+yaz&pg=PT59|title=Soul in Seoul: African American Popular Music and K-pop|first=Crystal S.|last=Anderson|date=25 August 2020|publisher=Univ. Press of Mississippi|isbn=9781496830111 |via=Google Books}}{{Cite web|url=https://music.apple.com/us/artist/alison-moyet/548342|title=Alison Moyet on Apple Music|website=Apple Music - Web Player}}{{Cite web|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=nwgEAAAAMBAJ&dq=new+wave+duo+yaz&pg=PA35|title=Billboard|date=4 September 1999|publisher=Nielsen Business Media, Inc.|via=Google Books}}{{Cite web|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=9uYwm-dwInwC&dq=yaz+british+duo+new+wave&pg=PA27|title=CMJ New Music Report|date=8 February 1999|publisher=CMJ Network, Inc.|via=Google Books}}{{Cite web|url=https://www.nzherald.co.nz/entertainment/alison-moyet-gets-real-i-aint-fing-playing-it/R37AQN56POZ4IPXXAPJ7FE36UQ/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231121064906/https://www.nzherald.co.nz/entertainment/alison-moyet-gets-real-i-aint-fing-playing-it/R37AQN56POZ4IPXXAPJ7FE36UQ/|url-status=live|archive-date=21 November 2023|title=Why Alison Moyet won't play her biggest hit|date=21 November 2023|url-access=subscription|website=[[NZ Herald]]}} "Besides, as she says, the trade-off is that she will perform the hits of Yazoo, whose early New Wave electronic sound has been hugely influential and therefore remains much more relevant."}} | years_active = {{hlist|1981–1983|2008|2011}} | label = {{hlist|[[Mute Records|Mute]]|[[Sire Records|Sire]]|[[Reprise Records|Reprise]]}} | current_members = | past_members = * [[Vince Clarke]] * [[Alison Moyet]] | website = {{URL|yazooinfo.com}} }} '''Yazoo''' (known as '''Yaz''' in North America) were an English [[synth-pop]] duo from [[Basildon]], [[Essex]], formed in late 1981 by [[Alison Moyet]] (vocals) and [[Vince Clarke]] (keyboards) after his departure from [[Depeche Mode]].{{Citation |last=Strong |first=Martin C. |author-link=Martin C. Strong |year=1998 |title=The Great Rock Discography |publisher=Giunti |page=935 |isbn=88-09-21522-2}} The pair released two albums, ''[[Upstairs at Eric's]]'' (1982) and ''[[You and Me Both]]'' (1983). Yazoo played a key role in shaping the emerging genre of synth-pop, and were particularly influential on the [[house music]] scene of the mid to late 1980s. The duo split in May 1983, with Moyet going on to launch a successful solo career and Clarke co-forming [[the Assembly]] and then [[Erasure (duo)|Erasure]]. Yazoo later reunited for a tour in 2008.{{cite news |first=Pete |last=Paphides |author-link=Peter Paphides |title=Back with his other Alf: Vince Clarke and Alison Moyet reunite for Yazoo |newspaper=[[The Times]] |location=London, England |date=18 April 2008}}{{cite web |first=Nix |last=Lowrey |title=Alison Moyet Interviewed: Only You – The Story & End of Yazoo |work=[[The Quietus]] |url= http://thequietus.com/articles/06189-alison-moyet-interview-yazoo |date=4 May 2011 |access-date=6 December 2013}}{{cite news |first=Kate |last=Burt |title=How We Met: Alison Moyet & Vince Clarke |url= https://www.independent.co.uk/extras/sunday-review/regulars/how-we-met-alison-moyet--vince-clarke-840984.html |newspaper=[[The Independent]] |date=8 June 2008 |access-date=11 June 2008 |url-status=bot: unknown |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20080611032013/http://www.independent.co.uk/extras/sunday-review/regulars/how-we-met-alison-moyet--vince-clarke-840984.html |archive-date=11 June 2008}} ==History== ===Formation and ''Upstairs at Eric's'' (1982)=== Clarke and Moyet grew up in Basildon and attended the same Saturday music school when they were eleven years old. Clarke was inspired to make [[electronic music]] after hearing [[Metropolitan Borough of Wirral|Wirral]] synth-pop group [[Orchestral Manoeuvres in the Dark]] (OMD). He became a co-founder of Depeche Mode, who in 1981 released an album and three Clarke-penned singles through [[Mute Records]].{{cite web|url=https://www.electronicsound.co.uk/features/long-reads/vince-clarke-game-of-drones/|title=Vince Clarke: Game of Drones|last=Ilic|first=Vel|date=14 September 2023|website=Electronic Sound|access-date=9 July 2024}}{{cite web|url=https://www.prsformusic.com/m-magazine/features/interview-vince-clarke|title=Vince Clarke|last=Nichols|first=Paul|date=27 December 2016|publisher=[[PRS for Music]]|access-date=24 August 2024}} Moyet spent her teens singing in various [[punk rock|punk]] and blues bands in her home town. She placed an advert in the UK weekly music magazine ''[[Melody Maker]]'' in late 1981 asking for musicians to form a "rootsy" blues band after her most recent group, the Screamin' Ab Dabs, had broken up.{{cite magazine|title=Classifieds|magazine=[[Melody Maker]]|page=34|date=14 November 1981}} "Brilliant female vocalist, experienced gigs/studio, seeks great rootsy soul/R&B band.—Alison, Basildon"{{cite magazine|first=Neil|last=Tennant|author-link=Neil Tennant|title=Yazoo!|magazine=[[Smash Hits]]|pages=4–5|date=13 May 1982}} Moyet was surprised when the only reply she received was from Clarke, who had recently stunned the music press by quitting Depeche Mode. Despite growing up nearby, Moyet and Clarke did not know each other. Moyet had been in the same class at school as [[Martin Gore]] and [[Andy Fletcher (musician)|Andy Fletcher]] who were Clark's bandmates in Depeche Mode.{{cite web|first=Ian|last=Wade|title=Changeling: Alison Moyet Interviewed|work=The Quietus|url=http://thequietus.com/articles/12247-alison-moyet-interview|date=16 May 2013|access-date=6 December 2013}} However, she had no prior contact with Clarke himself, remembering him as an outsider who, with his brothers, would wear t-shirts proclaiming their Christianity. Clarke had seen Moyet sing live a few times, as he was friends with her bandmate. Clarke wanted to maintain his relationship with Mute, saying in a 2008 interview, "When I left Depeche I wasn't sure I'd still have a record deal and was keen to play the label something of my own, so I wrote the song '[[Only You (Yazoo song)|Only You]]' but needed someone to demo it with. Alison happened to be advertising in a local paper so I called her." Believing that two band members were enough, Clarke opted for a "duo" configuration inspired by the likes of OMD and [[Soft Cell]].{{cite magazine|last=Earls|first=John|author-link=John Earls|date=7 February 2019|title=Stereo System|magazine=[[Classic Pop|Classic Pop Presents]]|edition=Synthpop|issue=13|pages=72–75|quote=[Clarke:] After Depeche, I thought, 'OK, I can do the music myself'... Thanks to groups like OMD and Soft Cell, it was obvious that being a duo could work. It's easier to collaborate with one person than it is with three.}} The pair came to the project with different tastes in music. In an early interview, Moyet stated that "I'm a traditionalist, I can't accept the fact of blues with synthesizers at all," while Clarke admitted to tolerating modern [[rhythm & blues|R&B]] outfits like [[Dr. Feelgood (band)|Dr. Feelgood]] but disliked traditional blues artists such as [[Muddy Waters]].{{cite magazine|first=Chris|last=Bohn|title=Blues a la Mode|magazine=[[NME]]|page=4 |date=17 April 1982}} Clarke took the "Only You" demo to Mute label boss [[Daniel Miller (music producer)|Daniel Miller]] but recalled that at first Miller appeared to be uninterested:
"I tried to give it to Daniel and he didn't show much interest ... I brought it in and put it on, and the whole time it was playing, Daniel was messing around with a synthesizer. He said he liked it, but carried on doing what he was doing—and that was it. Only when the publishers took an interest did he brighten up."
Mute asked the duo to record the song as a single and to make an album together. By this point Clarke had already written "[[Don't Go (Yazoo song)|Don't Go]]", but both he and Moyet felt it was too good to be the B-side of "Only You", so they quickly wrote the song "Situation" together for the single's B-side. According to Moyet, the name Yazoo was taken from the specialist blues record label [[Yazoo Records]].{{Citation|last=Miller|first=Jonathan|year=2004|title=Stripped: Depeche Mode|publisher=Omnibus Press|page=128|isbn=1-84449-415-2}} This decision led to a £3.5 million lawsuit threat by the label over the band's name and, coupled with the fact that the name Yazoo was already in use by a lesser known American rock band, the group was renamed Yaz for the North American market. "Only You" was released in the UK in March 1982 and rose to number two on the UK singles chart.{{cite book |title=British Hit Singles & Albums |title-link=British Hit Singles & Albums |publisher=Guinness World Records Ltd |year=2006 |isbn=978-1-904994-10-7 |editor-last=Roberts |editor-first=David |edition=19th |location=London, England |page=613}} The duo recorded their debut album at [[Blackwing Studios]] in southeast London, where Clarke had recorded Depeche Mode's album ''[[Speak & Spell (album)|Speak & Spell]]'' the previous year. As the studio had already been booked during the day by fellow Mute artist [[Fad Gadget]], Yazoo recorded most of the album during the early mornings.{{cite web |first=John |last=Freeman |title=Synthesizer Soul: Yazoo's Upstairs At Eric's 30 Years On |url=http://thequietus.com/articles/09800-yazoo-upstairs-at-erics |work=The Quietus |date=23 August 2012 |access-date=8 March 2018}} Clarke had expected that Miller would produce the album, but discovered that Miller was already otherwise occupied, so Blackwing studio owner [[Eric Radcliffe]] carried out production duties with Clarke and Moyet. The album was named ''[[Upstairs at Eric's]]'' in recognition of Radcliffe's input. "Don't Go" was released in July 1982 as the second single in the UK and also reached the top three of the UK charts. In North America, "Situation" had been a hit in the clubs in a version remixed by New York City-based DJ [[François Kevorkian]], and against the band's wishes, it was released as Yazoo's debut single in the US and Canada, where it reached number 73 on the [[Billboard Hot 100|''Billboard'' Hot 100]]. "Only You" was released as Yazoo's second single in North America and reached number 67.{{cite magazine |title=Yaz Chart History – Hot 100 |magazine=[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]] |url=https://www.billboard.com/artist/yaz/chart-history/hsi/ |access-date=8 March 2018}} ''Upstairs at Eric's'' was released in the UK in August 1982, peaking at number two on the UK Albums Chart and going on to sell more than 300,000 copies and achieving platinum status.{{cite web |title=BPI Awards – Certified Awards Search |url=https://www.bpi.co.uk/bpi-awards/ |access-date=8 March 2018 |archive-date=9 September 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170909233259/https://www.bpi.co.uk/bpi-awards/ |url-status=dead }} Type "Yazoo" into "Search BPI Awards" box and press "Enter". In the US, initial success was more modest and the album peaked at number 92 on the [[Billboard 200|''Billboard'' 200]] album chart,{{cite magazine |title=Yaz Chart History – Billboard 200 |magazine=[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]] |url=https://www.billboard.com/artist/yaz/chart-history/tlp/ |access-date=8 March 2018}} but by 1989, seven years after its release, word of mouth had helped to push the album to platinum status for sales of over one million copies.{{cite web |title=Gold & Platinum – RIAA | website=[[Recording Industry Association of America]] |url=https://www.riaa.com/gold-platinum/?tab_active=default-award&ar=yaz&ti=upstairs+at+eric%27s&lab=&genre=&format=&date_option=release&from=&to=&award=&type=&category=&adv=SEARCH#search_section |access-date=8 March 2018}} The duo played 24 dates in support of the album across Europe and North America. ===''You and Me Both'' and disbandment (1983)=== After releasing "[[The Other Side of Love]]" in the UK in November 1982, a non-album stopgap single that reached number 13 in the UK singles chart, the duo went back to Blackwing to record their second album. However, by now there was growing tension between the pair. Clarke had always seen ''Upstairs at Eric's'' as a one-off project and had to be persuaded to make another Yazoo record by his publishers, who felt it would not go down well if he was seen to walk out of a second band within a year of the first. Compounding this were issues of self-esteem for Moyet. At only 21 years of age, she was struggling to come to terms with being in the spotlight and the pressures of sudden fame, and she resented the fact that Clarke was leaving her to carry out all the promotional work for the records by herself.{{cite magazine |first=Paul |last=Colbert |title=Diary of a Somebody |magazine=Melody Maker |pages=24–25 |date=25 June 1983}} Unlike their first record, the second album was made over a longer period of four months and with Clarke and Moyet rarely in the studio together at the same time; Clarke would record instrumental tracks in the morning and Moyet would come in during the evening and record her vocals. A single, "[[Nobody's Diary]]", was released in May 1983 ahead of the album and reached number three in the UK chart, but within days of the single's release, Yazoo announced that they were splitting up due to personal development reasons.{{cite news |newspaper=NME |page=[https://www.worldradiohistory.com/UK/New-Musical-Express/1983/NME-1983-05-21.pdf 2]|title=Yazoo to split |date=21 May 1983}} The album, ironically titled ''You and Me Both'', was released in the UK in July 1983 and topped the UK album charts, a feat it would also achieve in New Zealand. However, with no further singles or live appearances to promote it, it did not sell as well as ''Upstairs at Eric's'', although it still achieved gold status in the UK for sales of 100,000 copies. In the US, ''You and Me Both'' peaked at number 69 on the ''Billboard'' 200. Reflecting in 2008 on the group's split, both Moyet and Clarke agreed that a lack of communication between the pair had been a major reason for the breakdown of the partnership. Moyet recalled that Clarke "was creatively very encouraging, very open to hearing my ideas for songs. The thing I found difficult was the lack of warmth. I wanted to feel more likeable, and you can't feel likeable if someone doesn't want to interact with you." Clarke admitted that "I lacked the life-skills of communication in a relationship. I felt confident in the studio, but starting a chat with somebody ..." He put it down to the fact that because the duo became popular so rapidly, there had never been any time to build up a personal relationship between them:
"It all happened very fast and because we hadn't been in a band for years, playing in clubs, it was very much just a working relationship—we never had the chance to bond. We never really knew each other. Not really ... The fact that we never talked, never socialised together, meant that when problems came up we didn't know how to communicate and sort things out."
Moyet added that their differing personalities had not helped matters, saying, "He was, I think, sad at the time after leaving Depeche and remote, a bit angry, but it was all internalised. Whereas I was this disaffected, slightly aggressive ex-punk rocker where nothing was internalised. I was probably quite difficult to be around." ===Legacy=== Following Yazoo's split, Clarke formed [[the Assembly]] with [[Eric Radcliffe]]. Intending to record a series of one-off singles featuring different vocalists, in the end the Assembly produced just one single, "[[Never Never (The Assembly song)|Never Never]]" with [[Feargal Sharkey]], before also splitting up. Around this time, Clarke also produced the album ''The Peter Pan Effect'' for singer [[Robert Marlow]], an old friend of both his and Moyet's. Clarke then teamed up with singer [[Andy Bell (singer)|Andy Bell]] to form the successful synth-pop duo [[Erasure (duo)|Erasure]]. Moyet spent several months out of the limelight before signing a deal with [[CBS Records International|CBS Records]] and embarking on a successful solo career. "Situation" was finally released as a single in the UK in 1990 in another remixed form, which was moderately successful, reaching number 14 on the UK singles chart. A compilation entitled ''[[Only Yazoo|Only Yazoo: The Best of]]'' was released in 1999 and was preceded by a re-release of Yazoo's debut single, "Only You", featuring a new remix of the title track and several more of "Don't Go". The band's output was book-ended with yet another release of "Situation", accompanied by many remixes. Clarke was chosen to remix Moyet's 1994 single "Whispering Your Name" and, with Erasure, Clarke and Moyet tried to record her single "This House" as a duet, but the project never happened because [[Sony Music]] would not permit it.{{Citation needed|date=June 2008}} The band's songs have appeared in a number of films and television shows. In 1988, "In My Room", "Ode to Boy" and "Only You" were used in the film ''[[The Chocolate War (film)|The Chocolate War]]'' (an adaption of [[The Chocolate War|the book]] of the same title). "Only You" was used in the film ''[[Napoleon Dynamite]]'', the BBC television series ''[[The Office (British TV series)|The Office]]'', the film ''[[Can't Hardly Wait]]'', the ''[[Fringe (TV series)|Fringe]]'' episode "[[Transilience Thought Unifier Model-11]]", ''[[The Americans]]'' episode "[[Dimebag (The Americans)|Dimebag]]" and several episodes in [[Once Upon a Time season 5|season five]] of ''[[Once Upon a Time (TV series)|Once Upon a Time]]''. A [[cover version]] of "Only You" by Joshua Radin was used in 2007 in a [[J. C. Penney]] commercial. Another cover of "Only You" was recorded by Selena Gomez for the 2017 Netflix television show ''[[13 Reasons Why]]''. "Don't Go" appeared in the BBC series ''[[I'm Alan Partridge]]'' and was used in the film ''[[Tango and Cash]]''. The song "Situation" was used in the 1990 TV movie ''[[Exile (1990 film)|Exile]]'' and was also used in a [[Nintendo]] commercial highlighting the classic edition of the [[Game Boy Advance SP]] and the NES games ported to it. In 2007, "Bring Your Love Down (Didn't I)" was used in ''[[The Sarah Silverman Program]]'' episode "[[List of The Sarah Silverman Program episodes|Not Without My Daughter]]".{{Citation needed|date=June 2008}} [[Anohni]], lead vocalist of [[Antony & the Johnsons]], talked with [[Terry Gross]] in February 2009 about recording the debut self-titled ''[[Hercules and Love Affair]]'' album. She said she had been asked by New York-based DJ Andy Butler to join the project and that the objective was (or became) "Let's sound as much like Yazoo as we can ... We loved Yazoo."{{Cite web|url=https://www.npr.org/templates/story/story.php?storyId=100162285|title=Antony Hegarty's Otherworldly Sound|website=NPR.org |date=3 February 2009 }} ===2008 reunion and 'Reconnected' tour=== {{Multiple image | align = right | image1 = Alison Moyet 346-0010-hinnerk-ruemenapf.jpg | width1 = 143 | alt1 = Alison Moyet performing on stage in 2013 | link1 = | caption1 = Moyet in 2013 | image2 = Vince Clarke 2011.jpg | width2 = 143 | alt2 = Vince Clarke performing on stage in 2011 | link2 = | caption2 = Clarke in 2011 }} Despite the long estrangement, Moyet had always harboured plans to perform the songs from ''You and Me Both'' live on stage, something that had never occurred, as the duo had split before the album was released. Toward the end of 2007, she had finished promoting her album ''[[The Turn (Alison Moyet album)|The Turn]]'' and had no immediate plans for more solo work, and aware that Mute were planning to issue remastered versions of Yazoo's albums, she e-mailed Clarke to see if he was interested in the idea of a reunion. Clarke welcomed her message, but replied that he was now committed to his current band Erasure and felt it would be disloyal to his musical partner Andy Bell if he returned to work with Moyet. However, shortly afterwards Bell told Clarke that he wanted to take a break from Erasure, causing Clarke to reconsider Moyet's proposal, and with a message sent via Mute label head Daniel Miller, he indicated that he was open to reuniting for live performances. Clarke disclosed that he had felt obliged to ask Bell if he had any objections to Clarke performing with Yazoo again: Bell's response had simply been to ask Clarke for tickets for the reunion shows. The first public indication that Yazoo was being revived was on 11 December 2007 when Erasure's website announced that an official Yazoo website and [[Myspace]] page were being set up.{{cite book |first=Jonathan |last=Miller |title=Stripped: Depeche Mode |publisher=[[Music Sales Group|Omnibus Press]] |location=London, England |edition=3rd revised |year=2008 |isbn=978-1-84772-444-1}} On 13 December, the [[Planet Sound]] music magazine pages on the UK's [[Teletext]] service on [[Channel 4]] exclusively revealed that both Yazoo albums were to be reissued and that the duo were planning to reform and play a gig in support of the albums' release.{{cite web|first=Bernard|last=van Isacker|title=Yazoo reunion for reissue albums and first live gig in 25 years|publisher=Side-Line|url=http://www.side-line.com/news_comments.php?id=27901_0_2_0_C|date=18 December 2007|access-date=4 November 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130906084012/http://www.side-line.com/news_comments.php?id=27901_0_2_0_C|archive-date=6 September 2013|url-status=dead}} On 20 January 2008, the new official Yazoo website confirmed that Clarke and Moyet would be reuniting to play five concerts across the UK in June 2008, preceded by a four-disc box set entitled ''[[In Your Room (Yazoo album)|In Your Room]]'', which would feature remastered stereo and [[5.1 surround sound]] mixes of the albums ''Upstairs at Eric's'' and ''You and Me Both'', a disc of [[A-side and B-side|B-side]]s and remixes and a DVD including new interviews with Clarke and Moyet and the videos for their five UK and US singles, along with video footage of television performances from 1982 and 1983.{{cite news |title=Pop duo Yazoo reunite for UK tour |work=[[BBC News]] |url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/entertainment/7205062.stm |date=23 January 2008 |access-date=4 November 2013}} Two [[Extended play|EP]]s available on vinyl and as [[music download|digital downloads]] were released to coincide with the box set, the ''[[Nobody's Diary#Nobody's Diary EP|Nobody's Diary EP]]'' released on 12 May 2008 featuring various remixes of the song (including one by Erasure's Andy Bell){{citation |title='Nobody's Diary' Exclusive Download Only Mix |publisher=Yazooinfo.com |url=http://www.yazooinfo.com/news_2008_04.html#n12 |date=11 April 2008 |access-date=4 November 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130715235204/http://yazooinfo.com/news_2008_04.html#n12 |archive-date=15 July 2013 |url-status=dead }} and the ''Reconnected'' EP released on 9 June 2008, which featured various Yazoo tracks remixed by different artists.{{citation |title=Reconnected EP |publisher=Yazooinfo.com |url=http://www.yazooinfo.com/news_2008_05.html#n30 |date=26 May 2008 |access-date=4 November 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130714020031/http://yazooinfo.com/news_2008_05.html#n30 |archive-date=14 July 2013 |url-status=dead }} Having re-established contact, Clarke and Moyet met on 8 April 2008 in a [[gentlemen's club|private members' club]] in London's [[Covent Garden]], with the occasion filmed by the press: it was the first time they had met since a mutual friend's wedding in the early 1990s. The promotion for the tour received moderate television coverage, including a performance on the prime-time [[BBC]] chat show ''[[Friday Night with Jonathan Ross]]'', broadcast in the UK on 16 May 2008.{{cite web |title=Friday Night with Jonathan Ross – Series 14, Episode 17 |publisher=[[BBC]] |url=http://www.bbc.co.uk/programmes/b00bbwg4 |date=16 May 2008 |access-date=4 November 2013}} The tour was rapidly expanded to include concerts in Europe and in the US, as well as extra dates in the UK. The 'Reconnected' tour, as it became known, began in [[Copenhagen]] on 26 May 2008, the same day as ''In Your Room'' was released.{{Citation|date=22 February 2008|title=Yazoo announces more European dates for 'Yazoo reunion Reconnected Tour'|periodical=Side-Line|url=http://www.side-line.com/news_comments.php?id=29494_0_2_1_C|access-date=25 May 2008|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081222051030/http://www.side-line.com/news_comments.php?id=29494_0_2_1_C|archive-date=22 December 2008|url-status=dead}} The concert of 10 July 2008 at the [[Orpheum Theatre (Los Angeles)|Orpheum Theatre]] in Los Angeles was recorded to be re-aired on [[Richard Blade]]'s [[Sirius Radio]] show.{{Citation|date=22 July 2008|title=US Yazoo concert to be broadcast on satellite radio|periodical=Side-Line|url=http://www.side-line.com/news_comments.php?id=33889_0_2_1_C|access-date=22 July 2008|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081222051058/http://www.side-line.com/news_comments.php?id=33889_0_2_1_C|archive-date=22 December 2008|url-status=dead}} Yazoo wrapped up the final two dates of the US tour by returning to New York City for the first time since October 1982. In an interview in May 2008 with the online magazine ''Side-Line'', Clarke said that there were plans to record the two London shows on the tour for a possible live album in the future.{{cite web|first=Bernard|last=van Isacker|title=Yazoo – It wasn't a well keened out marketing ploy!|publisher=Side-Line|url=http://www.side-line.com/interviews_comments.php?id=32146_0_16_0_C|date=30 May 2008|access-date=4 November 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130907001705/http://www.side-line.com/interviews_comments.php?id=32146_0_16_0_C|archive-date=7 September 2013|url-status=dead}} A double album titled ''[[Reconnected Live]]'', featuring tracks recorded on the "Reconnected" tour, was eventually released in September 2010.{{cite web|title=Yazoo confirms 'Reconnected Live' formats and tracklisting|publisher=yazooinfo.com|url=http://www.yazooinfo.com/news_2010_06.html|date=28 June 2010|access-date=4 November 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131211165805/http://www.yazooinfo.com/news_2010_06.html|archive-date=11 December 2013|url-status=dead}} On 14 May 2011, Moyet appeared as a guest on stage before Erasure's set on the second day of Mute Records' Short Circuit music festival at the [[Roundhouse (venue)|Roundhouse]] in London. She performed three Yazoo songs with Clarke, "Nobody's Diary", "Ode to Boy" and "Don't Go". Radcliffe]] * Yazoo | prev_title = | prev_year = | next_title = [[You and Me Both]] | next_year = 1983 | misc = {{Singles | name = Upstairs at Eric's | type = studio | single1 = [[Only You (Yazoo song)|Only You]] | single1date = 15 March 1982 (UK) | single2 = [[Don't Go (Yazoo song)|Don't Go]] | single2date = 2 July 1982 (UK) | single3 = [[Situation (song)|Situation]] | single3date = July 1982 (US/Canada) }} }} '''''Upstairs at Eric's''''' is the debut album by English [[synth-pop]] duo [[Yazoo (band)|Yazoo]] (known in North America as Yaz). It was released on 20 August 1982 by [[Mute Records]].{{cite magazine |title=Record News |magazine=[[Melody Maker]] |page=4 |date=21 August 1982}} It was produced by the band and [[Eric Radcliffe|E.C. Radcliffe]], with assistance from Mute label boss [[Daniel Miller (music producer)|Daniel Miller]] on some of the tracks. Named after producer Radcliffe's [[Blackwing Studios]] where the album was recorded, ''Upstairs at Eric's'' was preceded by two UK top-three singles, the ballad "[[Only You (Yazoo song)|Only You]]" and the more uptempo "[[Don't Go (Yazoo song)|Don't Go]]". The album reached number two on the [[UK Albums Chart]] and has been certified platinum by the [[British Phonographic Industry]] (BPI), denoting shipments in excess of 300,000 copies in the United Kingdom. Against the group's wishes, "[[Situation (song)|Situation]]", originally the [[A-side and B-side|B-side]] of "Only You" in the UK and Europe, was released as the band's debut single in the United States and Canada, where a remixed version of the song by [[disc jockey|DJ]] [[François Kevorkian]] reached number one on ''[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]''{{'s}} [[Hot Dance Club Songs|Club Play Singles]] chart. "Situation" peaked at number 73 on the US [[Billboard Hot 100|''Billboard'' Hot 100]], while it reached the top 40 in Canada, peaking at number 31. The North American version of the album subsequently replaced the remixed version of "Situation" for the UK album track "Tuesday". ''Upstairs at Eric's'' reached number 92 on the [[Billboard 200|''Billboard'' 200]] in the US and number 49 on ''[[RPM (magazine)|RPM]]''{{'s}} albums chart in Canada. == Recording and composition == Following the success of their debut single "Only You", Vince Clarke and Alison Moyet rapidly recorded the album to maintain their {{not a typo|high profile}}. As Clarke's only previous experience of a recording studio had been [[Blackwing Studios]] in south-east London, where he had made [[Depeche Mode]]'s debut album ''[[Speak & Spell (album)|Speak & Spell]]'', his immediate thought was to record Yazoo's album there as well: he said later, "I didn't know of any other studios, so I just assumed that Blackwing was the only studio I could record at". However, when the duo arrived at Blackwing they found that not only was Daniel Miller unavailable to produce the album, contrary to Clarke's expectations, but the main studios had already been booked out during the daytime by [[Fad Gadget]], another Mute label act. Instead Clarke and Moyet had to record the album in the early mornings with studio owner Eric (E.C.) Radcliffe overseeing most of the recording process, turning up around 5 or 6 a.m. and working until 11 a.m. each day in whichever of the two studio spaces were available at the time.{{cite web |first=John |last=Freeman |title=Synthesizer Soul: Yazoo's Upstairs at Eric's 30 Years On |url=http://thequietus.com/articles/09800-yazoo-upstairs-at-erics |work=[[The Quietus]] |date=23 August 2012 |access-date=2 December 2013}}{{cite book |first=Jonathan |last=Miller |title=Stripped: Depeche Mode |publisher=[[Music Sales Group|Omnibus Press]] |location=London, England |edition=3rd revised |year=2008 |isbn=978-1-84772-444-1}} On the 30th anniversary of ''Upstairs at Eric's'' in 2012 Clarke told ''[[The Quietus]]'' that there had been no grand plan for the album's creation:{{Blockquote|We just came together and it was a bit of a mish-mash really. There was no concept or theme running through the album; we were just messing about in the studio. Part of the charm of that album is a naivety. There really wasn't a profound concept that was running through the recording. I didn't really know what I was doing in the studio and Alison hadn't much experience of being in a recording studio, so everything was new. We'd make one sound and we'd think it was great and just stop there and wouldn't make any more sounds. It wasn't like we were continually honing or over-producing songs because everything at the time sounded fresh. That's why a lot of the tracks only have eight or nine elements to them.}} Clarke's compositions "I Before E Except After C" and "In My Room" explore the use of cut-up vocals, including his own spoken word voice. "I Before E Except After C" features both Moyet and the mother of producer Eric Radcliffe separately reading out the instruction manual for one of the pieces of studio equipment, with Moyet struggling to keep herself from laughing. Moyet later described how her song "Goodbye 70's" had been inspired by her disillusionment with how the late-1970s punk scene had turned out, saying, "'Goodbye 70's' is about punk and not caring how you were dressed, and then I discovered that so many of my friends that I'd thought it all really meant something to just saw it as another trend... That's what 'Goodbye 70's' was all about, about how sour the whole thing became."{{cite magazine |first=Don |last=Watson |title=What's It All About, Alfie? |magazine=[[NME]]|location=London, England |pages=6–7 |date=28 May 1983}} == Artwork == The album cover depicts two apparently male [[mannequins]] in a sparsely furnished [[loft]], facing each other over a table, with the lower part of the dummies' bodies seated on pushed back chairs while the upper portions are perched on the edges of the table. It was shot by photographer Joe Lyons at his first photo studio in north London, and he described how he had set up the shot:{{Quote|"I'd just shot some furniture for a furniture designer, and got paid with the furniture. I chose dummies and started work—a fortuitous series of events. I felt that the hi-tech furniture worked really well with the rough look of the room, and I put the cake—which was actually the top of my wedding cake—as a focus on the table."}} The original UK CD release of ''Upstairs at Eric's'' in 1986 featured a close-up of part of the original album cover. The set was released by [[Mute Records]] (in North America by [[Sire Records]]) on May 26, 2008, and contains four discs.{{cite web |url=http://www.yazooinfo.com/news.html |title=Yazoo (Vince Clarke & Alison Moyet) News |publisher=Yazooinfo.com |date=2012-08-31 |access-date=2015-04-29 }}{{Dead link|date=August 2025 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}[http://www.erasureinfo.com/news/index.html ] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080115204515/http://www.erasureinfo.com/news/index.html |date=January 15, 2008 }} ''In Your Room'' contains Yazoo's only two studio albums (''[[Upstairs at Eric's]]'' and ''[[You and Me Both]]'') in stereo and [[surround sound|5.1]] remasters. The fourth disc is a DVD containing the [[music video]]s for "Don't Go", "The Other Side of Love", "Nobody's Diary", "Situation" (1990 version) and "Only You" (1999 version). Clarke's current Erasure partner [[Andy Bell (singer)|Andy Bell]] contributed a new [[remix]] of "Nobody's Diary" to the ''[[Nobody's Diary|Nobody's Diary EP]]'', released prior to the box set. Afterwards there was also the release of the ''Reconnected EP''. ==Reunion concerts== The box set was issued in conjunction with a short Yazoo tour in Europe and the U.S. It was the first time band members [[Vince Clarke]] and [[Alison Moyet]] performed together in over twenty-five years and the first time any songs from ''You and Me Both'' were played live, as the duo split shortly before the release of that album in 1983. It was also the first time Yazoo toured North America. Many of them have never been played live. I'm looking forward to performing them with Alison for all the fans who've enjoyed our music through the years but never had a chance to see Yazoo in concert."}} Moyet has stated: {{cquote|"Playing this material live is not about revision for me, it is about finishing something we started – writing, recording, performing. [[synth-pop]] band [[Yazoo (band)|Yazoo]] (known in the US and Canada as Yaz). It was released on 5 July 1982{{cite magazine |title=Record News |magazine=[[New Musical Express]] |date=3 July 1982 |page=36 |issn=0028-6362}} as the second single from their debut album, ''[[Upstairs at Eric's]]'' (1982). The song peaked at number three on the [[UK Singles Chart]], becoming Yazoo's second top 5 hit. In the US, where the band was known as Yaz, the song was their second big hit on the [[Dance Club Songs|American dance chart]], where it spent two weeks at number one in October 1982. Their first American dance chart hit was "[[Situation (song)|Situation]]", which had also gone to number one on this chart earlier the same year. The [[music video]] for the song features band members [[Alison Moyet]] and [[Vince Clarke]] in a sort of haunted mansion with Clarke cast in the role of [[Victor Frankenstein]]. The song re-entered the UK Dance Chart on 13 December 2009 at number 30, peaking at number 15 on 2 January 2010. ==Critical reception== Adrian Thrills of ''[[NME]]'' picked "Don't Go" as the magazine's "single of the week" and described it as a "slice of melodrama that knocks the rest of this week's releases into a cocked hat in terms of impact and intensity". He added that, as the "first full exposition of their talent" following the "delightful" "[[Only You (Yazoo song)|Only You]]", "Don't Go" "builds busily to a strident crescendo as Clarke juggles with a shrill synth motif that jostles with Alf's booming, swelling vocals".{{cite magazine |last=Thrills |first=Adrian |title=Singles |magazine=[[New Musical Express]] |date=10 July 1982 |page=21 |issn=0028-6362}} Ian Birch of ''[[Smash Hits]]'' considered the song to be a "sharp successor" to "Only You". He commented: "Vince coaxes a sterling song out of his synthesizer while Alf balances its metallic clip with a deep, emotion-packed vocal that gets better with every hearing."{{cite magazine |last=Birch |first=Ian |title=Singles |magazine=[[Smash Hits]] |date=8 July 1982 |volume=4 |issue=14 |page=22 |issn=0260-3004}} Mark Cooper of ''[[Record Mirror]]'' described it as "a rather slight blues belter dignified by the singing and the synth break in the middle". He continued: "The combination of the voice and the machine is truly original and the B-side, 'Winter Kills', shows that Yazoo are capable of moods of substance."{{cite magazine |last=Cooper |first=Mark |title=Singles |magazine=[[Record Mirror]] |date=10 July 1982 |page=15 |issn=0144-5804}} ==Formats and track listings== * '''UK 7" single''' (Mute 7 YAZ 001) #"Don't Go" – 2:53 #"Winter Kills" – 4:02 * '''US 12" single''' (Sire 29886-0) #"Don't Go (Re-mix)" – 4:08 #"Don't Go (Re-re-mix)" – 4:20 #"Winter Kills (album version)" – 4:03 Note 1: "Winter Kills," the B-side to this single, is explicitly listed as "Not re-mixed" and "Not extended" on the album sleeve

'''''The Collection''''' is a two-disc compilation album by English [[synth-pop]] duo [[Yazoo (band)|Yazoo]], released under licence from [[Mute Records]] by Music Club Deluxe, a division of [[Demon Music Group]], in September 2012. '''''Four Pieces''''' is a deluxe vinyl [[box set]] by English [[synth-pop]] duo [[Yazoo (band)|Yazoo]], released on 26 October 2018 by [[Mute Records]]. Set in hardback book format and pressed on heavyweight black 180g vinyl, the collection includes remastered editions of the band's two studio albums along with remixes and [[BBC Radio 1|BBC]] sessions, some of which are previously unreleased. Due to popular demand, the box set has also been confirmed for release on CD.<ref>{{cite web |title=Yazoo Announce Four-Disc Retrospective Box Set |url=https://louderthanwar.com/yazoo-announce-four-disc-retrospective-box-set/ |website=Louder Than War |access-date=28 July 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=FOUR PIECES – A YAZOO COMPENDIUM 4-VINYL BOXSET |title=Yazoo Website |url=http://yazooinfo.com/ |website=Yazoo Official Website |access-date=28 July 2018}}</ref>
